name: Utah

law.summary: Sewer systems must report a Class 1 (significant) SSO to the Division of Water Quality orally within 24 hours and in writing within five days; Class 2 SSOs go only in the annual report. No duty to tell the public was found; local health departments issue water advisories.

citations.title: General Permit SSO Reporting Requirements
citations.quote: (1) A Class 1 SSO shall be reported orally within 24 hrs and with a written report submitted to the DWQ within five calendar days. Class 1 SSO's shall be included in the annual USMP report. (2) Class 2 SSOs shall be reported on an annual basis in the USMP annual report.
citations.deadline: 24 hours oral; five calendar days written; annual report by April 15

citations.title: Definition of Class 1 SSO
citations.quote: "Class 1 SSO" (Significant SSO) means a SSO or backup that is not caused by a private lateral obstruction or problem that: (a) effects more than five private structures; (b) affects one or more public, commercial or industrial structure(s); (c) may result in a public health risk to the general public; (d) has a spill volume that exceeds 5,000 gallons, excluding those in single private structures; or (e) discharges to Waters of the state.
citations.threshold: any SSO reaching waters of the state is Class 1

regulator_report.deadline: 24 hours oral; five calendar days written

bills_and_cases: No 2025-2026 Utah bill on public sewage-spill notice found (search only).

erule.notes: 188 Utah collection systems are registered in EPA's collection_system_permits.csv, but only one event (Timpanogos, 2026-08) is in SOBE. Whether Utah reports flow to EPA or stay in a DWQ system was not established.

statewide_feed.history: 1995 to date; 18 to 33 sewage rows a year
statewide_feed.start_end: discovery date and hour; no end
statewide_feed.notes: Partial coverage: only incidents called in to the DEQ spill hotline (DERR); most Class 1 SSOs reported to DWQ are not in it. Volume only in free text.

sso.notes: Sewage rows mix utility SSOs with dumping complaints; filter on title and summary.

beaches.program: DWQ recreational water monitoring (E. coli and HABs) with local health department advisories
beaches.notes: Warning E coli at 8 sites on 2026-11-03.

habs.program: DWQ HAB program; advisories by local health departments; habs.utah.gov map
habs.notes: Same layer as E. coli advisories.

shared_waters: Lake Powell and the Colorado River (AZ)
Bear Lake and Bear River (ID, WY)
San Juan River (NM, CO, Navajo Nation)

barriers.what: Class 1 SSO reports go to DWQ by phone and letter and are not published
barriers.note: Ask DWQ to publish them, or to route them into the Environmental Incidents layer.

barriers.what: No public notice duty for SSOs
habs.utah.gov returns 403 to scripts; eqspillsps.deq.utah.gov has an expired certificate

readiness.rationale: A public ArcGIS layer of spill-hotline incidents with dates, points and next-day updates; sewage rows need a text filter and cover only what is called in to DERR, so coverage is partial. HAB and E. coli advisories are a second machine-readable layer.

owner_questions: The Environmental Incidents layer holds only hotline calls (about 20 to 30 sewage rows a year): accept it as Utah's dated feed with a coverage note, or treat Utah as partial?
Free-text filtering: include private dumping and RV sewage complaints, or only utility releases?
Ask DWQ for Class 1 SSO reports (records request) to measure what the layer misses?
Incident summaries name staff and private addresses: show only title, date, county and point?
surprise: Utah's spill hotline log is a public ArcGIS layer updated within a day, with a point and a PDF for every incident since 1995, yet the Class 1 SSOs that sewer districts must phone in to the Division of Water Quality mostly never reach it.
